title: Harvey raises $550M at a $15.5B valuation, Lightspeed and Diffusion co-lead
subtitle: The legal AI vendor has crossed $400M in ARR and sells to 80 of the top 100 US law firms — the new round funds Harvey LAB, a benchmarking product for legal agents, and a post-trained open-weight model.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Harvey announced a $550 million round on September 9, 2026 at a $15.5 billion post-money valuation, co-led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Diffusion — a new firm co-founded by former Coatue investor Kris Fredrickson. The round also brought in Sapphire Ventures and Whale Rock as new investors, alongside returning capital from Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins, Andreessen Horowitz, Coatue, Conviction, Elad Gil, GIC, and Goldman Sachs Alternatives. Annual recurring revenue passed $400 million and has nearly doubled since March.

The unit economics behind the round are worth naming: Harvey now sells to 80 of the 100 highest-ranked US law firms and half of the Fortune 10. That is the highest documented penetration of a vertical AI product into a professional services market, and it is what the valuation is pricing — not general model capability, but the fact that Harvey has become the default legal-workflow layer at firms whose partners bill $2,000 an hour. The company said the money funds Harvey LAB, a benchmarking product for legal agents, and continued work on its first post-trained open-weight model, released earlier in the year.

The round also lands in a strange spot in the funding market. Vertical AI has spent 2026 being either dismissed as wrapper-work or bid up to horizontal-lab valuations, with little middle ground. Harvey's numbers argue for a third position — that a domain company with real ARR, sticky contracts, and an evaluations product of its own can command a valuation that used to be reserved for foundation-model labs. Whether that pattern extends beyond law will depend on whether comparable numbers show up in healthcare (Abridge), accounting, and engineering. The Cognition round at $47B valuation last week and this Harvey round are pointing in the same direction.

Takeaway for learners: the pattern here is domain expertise plus evaluations, not model training. Harvey did not out-train Anthropic or OpenAI — it built the workflows, the retrieval, the citation checking, and the benchmarks that let a partner trust an agent's output. If you are building for a regulated profession, that is the recipe: pair the models the labs sell you with evaluation infrastructure the customer would otherwise have to build themselves. Harvey LAB exists because law firms wanted to test agents against their own contracts; that is the shape of the moat.
